Description

Conditionally required IR MEL instrumentation support (upstream RequiredIfInstrumentation): typed attachment, recording-level commands and owned completion reports. The metadata child polls copied reports. Inherited common channel services are accessed through common Channel support. Only the published Normal and Debug recording levels are bound.

As_Channel

function As_Channel (Channel : Instrumentation_Channel) return IR.Channel.View

Creates a weak common Channel view while attached or enabled. Inherited KeepAlive, CommsTest and capabilities are accessed through common Channel support, not duplicated instrumentation methods. The view does not keep the typed owner alive, and closing the view does not close it.

Parameters
Channel

Attached or enabled typed owner.

Return Value

New weak common channel view.

Raised exceptions
Provider_Error

Closed/failed owner or native view creation failure.

Capabilities

function Capabilities (Channel : Instrumentation_Channel) return IR.Channel.Channel_Capability

Parameters

Return Value

Owned common channel capability snapshot.

Raised exceptions
Provider_Error

Invalid lifecycle or provider/native query or conversion failure.

Close

procedure Close (Channel : in out Instrumentation_Channel)

Idempotently closes the typed public owner and deactivates metadata consumption. Pending requests defer physical disable/detach until completion. Cleanup disables if enable was attempted, detaches and destroys the provider channel before draining bridge callbacks. Synchronous detach failure retains the owner for retry; uncertain orphaned cleanup retains the provider graph. Automatic finalization attempts non-raising cleanup, not guaranteed immediate unload.

Parameters
Channel

Typed owner to close; serialize against other uses.

Raised exceptions
Provider_Error

Disable/detach or native cleanup failure; handle may remain for retry.

Close

procedure Close (Request : in out Instrumentation_Request)

Idempotently closes the public request handle without terminating provider work. Pending completion retains the native graph independently of public owners. Finalization attempts this cleanup without raising; the Ada wrapper ignores native close status. Do not race Wait on this same owner.

Parameters
Request

Public request owner to close.

Instrumentation_Channel

type Instrumentation_Channel is limited private;

Limited typed owner, initially closed. Open attaches without enabling. Native child state retains Session/provider lifetime after public Session closure. A common weak view does not keep this owner alive. Finalization attempts non-raising cleanup and can retain resources when detach ownership is uncertain. Externally serialize operations on a shared Ada owner.

type Instrumentation_Config is private;

Owned attachment configuration for the conditionally required instrumentation channel; constructing it performs no provider work.

Instrumentation_Report

   Command_ID   : Interfaces.Unsigned_32;
   Size         : Interfaces.Unsigned_32;
   Timestamp_NS : Long_Long_Integer;
   Priority     : Instrumentation.Priority;
end record;

Canonical owned report used both for asynchronous command completion and metadata callbacks. The pinned declaration contains only these four fields, not a variable instrumentation-data payload.

Record fields
Command_ID

Provider report command identifier, preserving all 32 bits.

Size

Raw provider size field; the pinned header does not specify its units or relation to any payload length.

Timestamp_NS

Provider timestamp in nanoseconds; clock and epoch are unspecified.

Priority

Provider-reported Normal or Debug instrumentation level; unknown values fail conversion.

Instrumentation_Request

type Instrumentation_Request is limited private;

Limited public asynchronous-request owner. A private completion worker consumes the provider future once and caches the result while retaining the native channel, Session and provider code. Public request Close and finalization do not cancel provider work; a never-completing future can retain resources indefinitely. Finalization is non-raising.

Instrumentation_Result

type Instrumentation_Result is private;

Ada-owned terminal report or explicit rejection. Provider exceptions, null successful results, unknown priority/error values and native failures raise Provider Error rather than becoming a normal Rejected result. Values survive request closure.

Open

function Open (Parent : Session; Config : Instrumentation_Config) return Instrumentation_Channel

Attaches and verifies an InstrumentationChannel and its advertised instrumentation capability; no owner escapes on failure. This interface is conditionally required only for providers supporting instrumentation. Capabilities, common services and metadata registration are available while attached; instrumentation Submit requires explicit Enable. Native configuration text must be UTF-8 without embedded NUL. Failure cleanup retains the native graph if detach is uncertain.

Parameters
Parent

Open IR Session supplying the child provider channel.

Config

Complete typed attachment configuration.

Return Value

Attached, not yet enabled, limited channel owner.

Raised exceptions
Provider_Error

Closed Session, invalid text, provider attach/type/capability failure or native failure.

Priority

type Priority is (Normal, Debug);

Exactly the two upstream instrumentation data-recording levels: Normal = 0 and Debug = 1. No additional levels or sentinel are defined.

Enumeration Literal
Normal

Normal instrumentation recording level, upstream numeric value zero.

Debug

Debug instrumentation recording level, upstream numeric value one.

function Report (Result : Instrumentation_Result) return Instrumentation_Report

Accesses the report of a terminal result. Requires Status equal to Success; enabled precondition checking raises Assertion Error on violation. The accessor body does not add an outcome check.

Parameters
Result

Owned terminal result satisfying the declared outcome precondition.

Return Value

function Status (Result : Instrumentation_Result) return Instrumentation_Outcome

Returns the terminal outcome stored in the result.

Parameters

Owned terminal instrumentation result.

Return Value

Submit

function Submit
  (Channel : Instrumentation_Channel; Command : Instrumentation_Level_Command)
   return Instrumentation_Request

Submits the supplied command only while the typed channel is enabled; does not implicitly Enable. Copies command values synchronously and returns a request handle, not proof of acceptance or completion. The native provider send runs outside the lifecycle lock so synchronous metadata callbacks can proceed. A pending request retains provider resources independently after public channel and Session closure.

Parameters
Channel

Enabled typed instrumentation owner; serialize application lifecycle operations.

Command

Command identifier and one of the two supported priority levels.

Return Value

Open limited request handle for later Wait.

Raised exceptions
Provider_Error

Closed/not-enabled channel, provider send exception or native failure.

Resource_Exhausted

Shared asynchronous-request admission limit reached.

Wait

function Wait
  (Request : Instrumentation_Request; Timeout_Milliseconds : Natural)
   return Instrumentation_Result

Waits for a terminal result without consuming the request. Timeout is not cancellation; later Wait may complete, and repeated terminal waits return the identical cached result. Explicit provider rejection is returned separately from provider exceptions or native failures. Rejection text is recovered completely by a checked cached retry if necessary; invalid UTF-8/NUL text receives a native fallback. Close must not race Wait on the same request.

Parameters
Request

Open public instrumentation request.

Timeout_Milliseconds

Maximum wait in milliseconds; zero polls.

Return Value

Owned report or explicit rejection.

Raised exceptions
Timeout_Error

Future has not completed within the wait; request remains open.

Provider_Error

Closed request, provider exception, invalid terminal result, or native/deferred-cleanup failure.

Description

Owned polling of four image metadata callback families: bad pixels, line-of-sight report, line-of-sight Euler and navigation response. Other upstream callbacks are not bound by Open. Payloads are copied at the native callback boundary and again into safe Ada values; no provider pointer is exposed. Optional NUC_TempData has a separate opt-in owner, NUC_Stream, so Open is unaffected by providers without NUC support. CameraCommandResp (@RequiredIfCameraCtrl) likewise has its own opt-in owner, Camera_Response_Stream, optional OpticalDistortionMap has its own opt-in owner, Optical_Distortion_Map_Stream, and LineOfSightQuaternion (@RequiredIfLOSQuaternion) has its own opt-in owner, Line_Of_Sight_Quaternion_Stream; Open never registers any of them.

Azimuth_Elevation

type Azimuth_Elevation is record
   Azimuth_Rad, Elevation_Rad : Long_Float;
end record;

Azimuth/elevation representation based on pinned AMS Math AzEl. Angle components are radians; the containing rate field must be distinguished from angles.

Record fields
Azimuth_Rad

Azimuth component; radians for an angle. The pointing-rate field has no explicitly documented time denominator upstream.

Elevation_Rad

Elevation component; radians for an angle. The pointing-rate field has no explicitly documented time denominator upstream.

type NUC_Stream is limited private;

Limited opt-in owner of ImageChannel @Optional NUC_TempData reception, independent of Metadata_Stream. Close deactivates consumption, not provider callback registration; finalization attempts non-raising cleanup. Serialize operations on the same owner.

Open

function Open
  (Stream : AMS.MEL.IR.Image_Stream; Queue_Capacity : Positive) return Metadata_Stream

Registers all four supported callbacks on an attached or running image stream, once per image stream, including after registration failure. Prefer registration before Start to avoid missing early events. A failed or unsupported registration raises Provider Error and publishes no metadata owner; already registered callbacks retain inactive state until provider-channel destruction because upstream supplies no unregister operation. All kinds share one bounded drop-incoming queue, ordered by successful enqueue under its mutex, not by timestamps or concurrent callback entry order. Closing metadata does not close the image stream.

Parameters
Stream

Owning image stream, not stopping, stopped or failed.

Queue_Capacity

Maximum number of queued events across all four kinds.

Return Value

Limited metadata-consumption owner.

Raised exceptions
Provider_Error

Closed/ineligible stream, repeated registration attempt, registration rejection/exception or native failure.

Open_Camera_Response

function Open_Camera_Response
  (Stream : AMS.MEL.IR.Image_Stream; Queue_Capacity : Positive) return Camera_Response_Stream

Registers the upstream ImageChannel CameraCommandResp callback once per image stream, including after failure. Registration may deliver synchronously. Failure publishes no owner; the retained callback stays inactive because upstream has no unregister. Responses are copied before the callback returns into one bounded drop-incoming queue; the owner stops with the stream. Delivery never proves a CameraCommand request completed.

Parameters
Stream

Attached or running image stream.

Queue_Capacity

Maximum number of queued responses.

Return Value

Limited CameraCommandResp consumption owner.

Raised exceptions

.MEL.IR.Camera.Not_Supported Provider answered NotSupported.

Provider_Error

Closed/ineligible stream, repeated attempt, other registration failure or exception, or native failure.

No normalization or other validity rule is applied. The owner stops with the stream.

Only the documented Mono8 single-band receive subset is supported, not optional upstream image processing or pixel-format conversion.

Acquire_Frame

  (Object : AMS.MEL.IR.Image_Stream; Timeout_Milliseconds : Natural := 0) return Frame_Lease

Close

procedure Close (Frame : in out Frame_Lease)

Closes the lease and invalidates its borrowed payload, also on provider-release failure. An already-closed lease is a no-op. The retained buffer is returned through the published Buffer release operation when successful. Provider failure or exception makes ownership uncertain: the bridge deliberately retains the provider graph, exact buffer object and host memory to avoid unsafe reuse or unload. This is not successful buffer release; the failed release is not automatically retried. Explicit Close reports failure, whereas automatic finalization suppresses it and can retain resources for safety. Final-child closure may perform deferred channel cleanup. Do not race Close with a borrow, copy, or another operation on this same lease.

Parameters
Frame

Lease consumed by this operation; its payload count becomes zero.

Raised exceptions
Provider_Error

Native buffer release or deferred cleanup did not complete safely.

Frame_Lease

type Frame_Lease is limited private;

Limited owner of one native snapshot retaining a provider-owned registered host buffer. The Frame Lease borrowed path performs no bulk image-payload copy from the MEL provider's registered host buffer into Ada. This is not end-to-end sensor zero-copy: pinned Squall copies UDP bytes into that host buffer; no DMA or kernel/network-stack zero-copy is claimed. Small metadata is copied at acquisition. A held lease keeps a provider buffer checked out; slow consumers cause backpressure or possible provider drops. Public stream/Session closure can be logical while physical teardown remains deferred behind leases, requests and release obligations. Closing the final child can trigger retained cleanup. Finalization is non-raising and can deliberately retain resources after uncertain release. Do not race lifecycle operations on a shared Ada object. Independent already-acquired leases may be processed separately; the stream still supports only one receive/acquire consumer.

Full_Frame

type Full_Frame is private;

Ada-owned complete frame snapshot: copied header, ordered flags, inertial/navigation sequences and pixel bytes. Unlike the smaller legacy IR Frame, this retains contributing-sensor identity and detailed navigation metadata. Returned snapshots survive stream, Session and provider closure.

Receive

function Receive
  (Object : AMS.MEL.IR.Image_Stream; Timeout_Milliseconds : Natural := 0) return Full_Frame

A control-only attachment raises Provider_Error with a control-only diagnostic; enabling that channel never makes sample access available. Receives a complete frame by copying header metadata and the entire pixel payload into Ada-owned storage, then closing the temporary native snapshot before return. The result survives stream, Session and provider closure. Pixels makes another independent copy. This exposes more metadata than legacy IR Receive, but performs no pixel decoding or conversion. Only Mono8 single-band nonempty dimensions and validated host-buffer spans are accepted; malformed provider frames are discarded by the native callback. At most one receive/acquire consumer may use a stream at once. Externally serialize lifecycle operations on a shared Ada owner. Timeout does not stop the stream. The private snapshot cleanup helper ignores native release status; explicit lease Close is the reporting path for release failures.

function Wait
  (Request : Navigation_Request; Timeout_Milliseconds : Natural) return Navigation_Result

Waits for a cached terminal result without consuming the request. Timeout is not cancellation; later waits may obtain completion and repeated terminal waits return the cached result. With_Pixels

procedure With_Pixels
  (Frame : Frame_Lease; Process : not null access procedure (Pixels : AMS.MEL.IR.Pixel_Array))

Synchronously invokes Process with a read-only-by-contract array aliasing native/provider storage, without a bulk payload copy. Array bounds are one through the byte count (one through zero if empty). The borrow ends when Process returns or raises: do not retain an address, slice, view or access object beyond that invocation. Keep the owning lease open throughout processing and do not race its Close. An exception from Process propagates without consuming the lease. Requires an open lease; enabled precondition checking raises Assertion Error on violation, while the body separately raises Provider Error for a closed handle or invalid payload address. No general thread safety or callback-quiescence guarantee is implied.

Parameters
Frame

Open owning lease which must remain open throughout Process.

Process

Synchronous read-only processor; must not retain any reference to borrowed storage.

Description

Independently owned RF administrative interface, separate from DataMEL and C2MEL. State commands use the provider's UCI status-control interface and the shared Common MEL state enumeration; no separate RF state model is introduced. Acceptance is not evidence of a physical state transition. Externally serialize operations on each owner, including closure and finalization. This package does not provide concurrent-handle protection.

Admin_MEL

type Admin_MEL is limited private;

Unique limited controlled owner of an AdminMEL and its provider-library reference. A default-initialized owner is closed. Explicit Close reports failures; finalization attempts closure without propagating exceptions. Native shutdown failure permanently retains the provider/library graph rather than destroying objects or unloading code at an uncertain boundary.

Close

procedure Close (Object : in out Admin_MEL)

Consume the public handle before invoking provider shutdown once. Closing an already closed owner is harmless. On success, destroy the AdminMEL before dropping its library reference; other library references may still prevent unloading. If shutdown throws, raise a provider error but leave the public owner closed and retain the complete native graph for process lifetime. A later Close does not retry that failed shutdown. Finalization follows the same native retention policy without propagating exceptions.

Parameters
Object

Owner to close; serialize against all other owner operations.

Command_State

function Command_State (Object : Admin_MEL; State : AMS.MEL.Status.MFA_State) return Boolean

Obtain fresh shared UCI and status-control owners and call upstream StatusControl::commandState. All fifteen Common MEL representations 0 through 14 are accepted by bridge validation, including the unset, Unknown and Degraded; provider support and acceptance remain separate. There is no bridge transition table, status polling or completion wait. Closed owners, null required provider interfaces, provider exceptions or malformed native Boolean results raise a provider error, not False.

Parameters

Open administrative owner; externally serialize its use.

State

Shared MFA state command, mapped by its checked enumeration representation.

Return Value

Embedded NUL in either input raises a constraint error before allocation of temporary C strings or any provider call. Temporary strings are freed on both normal and exceptional exits. Native loading, symbol lookup, allocation, null-factory-result and factory-exception failures raise a provider error; no open owner is returned on those failures.

Add_RX_Job_Intervals

procedure Add_RX_Job_Intervals (Object : in out Job; Intervals : RX_Job_Interval_List)

Synchronously serialize current safe values through native contract version 16, including mixed RX/TX. Historical v1-v15 contracts retain frozen layouts/domains: v16 uses the v8 base, TX-v3 and modulation-v5 plus context, not interchangeable array strides. Full-batch structural validation and local copied-value preparation precede one unlocked provider Add, including empty batches. Ordered intervals/events and duplicates survive. Borrowed transient Ada/C backing lasts through the call; native values own copies (native buffer copies share fresh sample vectors). Invalid final configuration raises Constraint Error before provider Add; lifecycle, registration and provider failures raise Provider Error. Add requires an open Job before any Finalize/full Cancel attempt, even if that attempt failed. Enabled reporting requires usable prior registration; no delivery guarantee. Externally serialize all same-Job calls/Close. No automatic retry: provider may mutate before throwing, and normal void return proves neither scheduling nor event execution/RF emission. Snapshot remains unchanged.

Parameters
Object

Open Job with Add admission still available.

Intervals

Complete owned ordered batch; not consumed by submission.

procedure Close (Object : in out C2_MEL)

Consume the public handle; repeated closure is harmless. With no child claims, invoke shutdown once, destroy C2, then drop its library reference. Otherwise defer shutdown until the final child releases its claim. New child admission stops at closure; existing children remain retained. A throwing shutdown raises a provider error on a synchronous cleanup path and permanently retains the complete graph without retry. Detached cleanup cannot report that error. Finalization uses non-raising cleanup instead.

Parameters

Close

procedure Close (Object : in out Job)

Idempotently consume the public owner, without implicit Finalize or Cancel. With no pending finalize work, release JobDetail, then provider VA, then the sibling C2 claim; report synchronous deferred shutdown failure as a provider error after closure. With pending work, do not wait: its worker retains the graph and DSO until completion, potentially indefinitely. A throwing shutdown retains the uncertain C2/library graph without retry; detached cleanup cannot report it. Controlled finalization never raises. Ada-owned Claim-time snapshots remain unchanged and readable after Close.

Parameters

Job owner to consume; externally serialize with its other calls.

Finalize_Job

procedure Finalize_Job (Object : in out Job)

Synchronously invoke provider finalize once, indicating that Job population is finished; hand its future to one native completion worker. Normal return means invocation/worker setup succeeded, not future completion or physical RF activation. Once invocation is attempted, repeated success returns normally and repeated synchronous failure raises the cached provider error without resending. An invalid future also raises a provider error. Bridge allocation failure before invocation does not consume the provider attempt. Cancel attempted first prohibits a new Finalize, even if Cancel returned False or raised; an already attempted Finalize remains repeatable from cache after Cancel. Future exceptions are reported by status Wait instead. Post-invocation worker failure retains future/provider/library state.

Parameters
Object

Open Job; externally serialize all same-Job calls and Close.

Flush_Job

procedure Flush_Job (Object : in out Job)

Synchronously call provider flush once per admitted invocation, requesting buffered intervals be sent. Allowed only before any Finalize/full Cancel attempt, even a failed attempt. Does not Finalize or alter copied snapshots. Provider failures raise Provider Error with no retry; mutation may precede a throw. Normal void return does not prove delivery, scheduling or RF execution. No status registration required.

Parameters
Object

Open Job; externally serialize same-Job calls and Close.

type Modulation_Config is private;

Ada-owned copyable tagged configuration, defaulting to Tone. Bridge kinds 0/1/2/3/4/5/6/7 select Tone, PhaseCode, LinearFrequencyModulation, OnOffKeying, CpfskPulse, CustomWaveform, WaveformBuffer and WaveformStream. These tags are not C++ variant positions: the first seven select an inner CommonModulations alternative inside Modulation; Stream selects the outer WaveformStream alternative directly. Cached/extension alternatives are not exposed. Only the active payload is serialized/validated. Scalars and arrays are copied; native buffer copies share their fresh sample allocation, not caller storage. Native double conversion preserves signed zero, infinities and NaN classification, not NaN payload bits. No normalization, waveform synthesis, frequency-domain conversion or provider capability guarantee follows from construction. All active definitions, including unused ones, validate before provider Add. Presence belongs independently to interval tables and TX reference collections.

RX_Element_Group_Config

type RX_Element_Group_Config is private;

TX JobRequest requirements only; this does not execute a TX interval. Power is exact provider-defined TxPowerLevel, not a TxPowerModeID.

RX_Job_Interval_Config

type RX_Job_Interval_Config is private;

Copyable Ada-owned interval configuration, now supporting both ordered RX and TX events despite the historical RX name. No resource allocation or scheduling. Default collections are empty, status Never, execution Normal, power mode zero; TX events, modulations, endpoint connections, product parameters and user context each have independent absent/present-empty/present-nonempty configuration states. Absence skips the corresponding native setter; native defaults can equal an explicit empty value, so provider-observable distinction is not guaranteed. Set/append operations own copies; no manual Close or provider pointer escapes. Upstream sequence nonoverlap, switching time, event-end/sequence duration, quantization and hardware constraints remain application/provider obligations; the bridge does not implement a scheduler or infer these relationships.

RX_Job_Interval_List

type RX_Job_Interval_List is private;

Owned ordered interval values, initially empty; copies are independent. Append retains duplicates; Add submits in list order, not interval-ID sort order.

RX_Receive_Event_Config

type RX_Receive_Event_Config is private;

Copyable Ada-owned RX event values, independent of subsequent edits to copies. Defaults are zero scalar fields, empty label/groups/polarization, Normal execution, Inhibit Event termination and False correction/delay/channelization. Stabilization index is always present and initially zero, not optional. Hold and termination counts default to zero. Add validates the whole batch before provider Add: UTF-8 labels without NUL, collection structure, enum domains and size t representability, not group membership or physical ranges. Floating values become native double without normalization or finite checks; IEEE signed zero, infinity and NaN classification survive, not NaN payload bits. Configuration is not execution, beam steering or cancellation. Provider capabilities and interpretation remain provider-defined. RX adds sample frequency, AGC counts and maximum extension; pulse settings are absent until Set, leaving upstream default settings when omitted.

Copy and validate requirements before provider entry, then create each command by label, require its selected RX/TX mode, populate requirements and call requestJob once. At least one total group is required; RX-only, TX-only and mixed requests are bridge inputs, not provider support claims. Labels must be UTF-8 without NUL. Validation/preparation failure publishes no request. A mode mismatch or synchronous native/provider failure raises a provider error; provider command mutations may precede a later exception, so this is not a provider rollback guarantee. Post-send worker/publication failure retains the future and graph. No physical RF activity is promised.

Parameters

Open aperture with C2 child admission still open; serialize submission with other owner calls and Close.

Config

Owned values copied synchronously, with no retained caller spans.

Return Value

Open asynchronous request, not a scheduling acceptance result.

TX_Transmit_Event_Config

type TX_Transmit_Event_Config is private;

Copyable Ada-owned TX event values, independent of subsequent edits to copies. Defaults are zero scalar fields, empty label/groups/polarization, Normal execution, Inhibit Event termination and False correction/delay/channelization. Stabilization index is always present and initially zero, not optional. Hold and termination counts default to zero. Add validates the whole batch before provider Add: UTF-8 labels without NUL, collection structure, enum domains and size t representability, not group membership or physical ranges. Floating values become native double without normalization or finite checks; IEEE signed zero, infinity and NaN classification survive, not NaN payload bits. Configuration is not execution, beam steering or cancellation. Provider capabilities and interpretation remain provider-defined. TX adds attenuation in dB and rise/fall durations, all initially zero. Modulation references are absent by default, retaining upstream {-1}. TX attenuation is neither TX Power Level nor an interval TX Power Mode ID; no RX sample frequency, AGC or pulse-detection configuration is exposed.

Description

Four inbound callback families, not outbound RequestFor sends. Required Track reports, advertised candidate messages and two optional callbacks share one bounded drop-incoming FIFO ordered by successful enqueue, not provider timestamps. Native callbacks never invoke Ada. Positive behavior is mock-qualified; pinned Squall cannot attach this Track channel.

Description

Asynchronous RF receive creation and bounded delivery of copied callback products. The eight supported integer/VITA formats use native v9 metadata; no DSP, RDMA setup, physical reception or provider-wide callback quiescence is promised. Limited owners require explicit Close, with non-raising finalization fallback.

Assigned_Data_Format

function Assigned_Data_Format (Object : Endpoint) return Job_Data_Format

Read the cached assigned provider format. Creation checks equality with the requested supported format before callback registration.

Parameters

Return Value

One of formats 0 through 7 after successful Claim; no conversion or broader upstream support is implied.

Claim

function Claim (Request : Create_Request'Class) return Endpoint

Transfer successful unclaimed creation to exactly one endpoint and register its data-ready callback. Pending Claim raises Timeout Error; failed, already-claimed or registration-failed requests raise Provider Error. A registration failure is cached and is not retried. Callback state is ready before registration, allowing synchronous callbacks. The exact registered std::function lvalue, callback state and provider DSO remain permanently retained: providers may keep a reference or move the callable. This shell owns neither DataMEL nor endpoint nor event payloads.

Parameters
Request

Open successful request; only one Claim may succeed.

Return Value

Unique open endpoint with the requested format verified against the assigned format; not proof of reception.

Close

procedure Close (Request : in out Create_Request)

Idempotently abandon the public request without cancelling the future. A pending worker retains the provider graph until settlement; an abandoned successful unclaimed endpoint is destroyed without callback registration. A claimed endpoint remains independently owned. Explicit closure reports native failures; automatic finalization is non-raising.

Parameters
Request

Owner consumed by closure; do not race its destruction with Wait or Claim.

Close

procedure Close (Object : in out Endpoint)

Idempotently consume the endpoint owner. Native logical closure discards queued products and wakes receivers before draining admitted bridge callback bodies; only then is the provider endpoint destroyed and its parent claim released. This drain is not provider-wide callback quiescence. Late callbacks take the stopped path before payload access. The permanent callable/state/DSO shell is not freed at Close. Failure to establish safe drain retains endpoint and claim; throwing parent shutdown permanently retains its provider graph. Delivered Events remain usable.

Parameters
Object

Endpoint owner to close; externally serialize wrapper destruction against other operations. Explicit failures raise Provider Error; finalization does not propagate them.

Close

procedure Close (Value : in out Event)

Idempotently release the sole native copied event and clear borrowed sample/packet addresses and count. Cached ID, format and Ada metadata remain stored; previously returned metadata and explicit payload copies remain independent. Externally serialize all event access with closure. Automatic finalization attempts the same release without propagating exceptions.

Event owner consumed; no provider sample buffer or endpoint is destroyed here.

The event remains usable after callback return and endpoint/DataMEL closure. Wrong format raises Constraint Error even for empty events; out-of-range Index raises Constraint Error and a closed event raises Provider Error. Externally serialize with Event Close/finalization and do not close the event in Process.

Parameters
Value

Open AMS VITA Small event owning the packet bytes.

Index

One-based packet-object position; must not exceed the packet count. An empty event has no valid index.

Process

Synchronous procedure receiving a one-based raw byte array only during this call. Do not retain addresses or borrow across tasks; application exceptions propagate.

Description

Description

Shared channel capability snapshots and the weak common-channel facade. Capability values describe provider reports, not a promise that the Ada bridge implements every advertised operation. Reading metadata support does not register a callback. Snapshots own their strings and collections independently of the provider, Session and typed channel.

Description

Outbound TrackDataUpdate under the upstream track-update condition, which is distinct from basic Track support. Requires Enabled Track. Positive execution is mock-qualified only; pinned Squall cannot attach Track. Bridge copies kinematics/covariance, performing no estimation, coordinate transformation, normalization or operational-incorporation verification.

Description

Owned values of the pinned upstream @Optional OpticalDistortionMap, received through the opt-in Optical_Distortion_Map_Stream owner of AMS.MEL.IR.Image.Metadata. Every published getter is copied: five unsigned 32-bit values, four double extrema and the complete FRD and RowCol collections. Values are independent of the native event, image stream, Session and provider library. The two collections are independent of each other and of the scalar dimensions: no length equality or product relation is assumed and no element is inferred. Long_Float components carry the provider IEEE doubles unchanged: finite, negative and signed-zero values are exact. Infinity and NaN are also carried unchanged, never replaced by zero or a substitute, but they are not valid Ada scalar values: callers must test them with 'Valid or IEEE comparisons before checked arithmetic. NaN payload bits are not promised.

AMS.MEL.IR.Line_Of_Sight_Quaternion

Entities

Exceptions

  • Not_Supported

Record Types

  • Line_Of_Sight_Value

Subtypes

  • Forward_Right_Down
  • Quaternion

Description

Owned values of the pinned upstream @RequiredIfLOSQuaternion LineOfSightQuaternion, received through the opt-in Line_Of_Sight_Quaternion_Stream owner of AMS.MEL.IR.Image.Metadata. Every published getter is copied exactly once: the signed nanosecond time, the X, Y, Z, W quaternion and the forward, right, down rotation rates. Values are independent of the native event, image stream, Session and provider library. The bridge supplies data only: it does not normalize the quaternion, canonicalize its sign, reorder its components, convert it to Euler angles, convert coordinate frames, infer a time epoch or clamp rates. Receipt is not evidence that the attitude is normalized, accurate or suitable for an independent pointing calculation. Long_Float components carry the provider IEEE doubles unchanged: finite, negative, subnormal, extreme and signed-zero values are exact. Infinity and NaN are also carried unchanged, never replaced by zero or a substitute, but they are not valid Ada scalar values. Only the private conversion and receive path disable the optional floating validity checks; a caller compiled with floating validity checks enabled (for example GNAT -gnatVa) may raise Constraint_Error when it copies or passes such a component as a scalar, so test components with 'Valid or IEEE comparisons before checked use. NaN payload bits are not promised.

Forward_Right_Down

subtype Forward_Right_Down is AMS.MEL.IR.Optical_Distortion_Map.Forward_Right_Down;

The canonical ForwardRightDown record, components Forward, Right and Down from upstream getForward/getRight/getDown. Here it holds rotation rates about the image coordinate frame axes, in radians per second; rates are not clamped or rescaled.

Line_Of_Sight_Value

type Line_Of_Sight_Value is record
   System_Time_NS : Long_Long_Integer := 0;
   Q_XYZW         : Quaternion := (others => 0.0);
   PQR_RPS        : Forward_Right_Down := (others => 0.0);
end record;

Complete owned LineOfSightQuaternion. The default value equals the upstream default: zero time, zero quaternion and zero rates.

Record fields
System_Time_NS

Time of validity in signed nanoseconds, from getSystemTime().count(); the full 64-bit range is kept and no clock or epoch is specified or inferred.

Q_XYZW

Line-of-sight quaternion in X, Y, Z, W order, from getQ_xyzw, in the upstream navigation coordinate frame; not normalized or sign-canonicalized.

PQR_RPS

Rotation rates about the image-frame forward, right and down axes in radians per second, from getPqr_rps; not clamped.

Not_Supported

Not_Supported : exception;

The provider answered NotSupported for the LineOfSightQuaternion registration, so it does not provide quaternion line of sight. The other Image metadata owners of the same stream are unaffected.

Quaternion

subtype Quaternion is AMS.MEL.IR.Image.Quaternion;

The canonical Image quaternion record, components X, Y, Z and W from upstream getQuaternionX/Y/Z/W in that order. Here it is the line-of-sight rotation in the upstream navigation coordinate frame (North/East/Down relative to wander North). It is not normalized and its sign is not canonicalized: q and -q stay distinct values.

Description

Close

procedure Close (Channel : in out Health_Channel)

Idempotently closes the typed public owner, deactivating metadata consumption. Native cleanup disables if enable was attempted and detaches before destroying the provider channel, then drains bridge callbacks. Pending inherited common requests can defer physical cleanup after logical Close. A synchronous detach failure retains ownership for retry; uncertain deferred failure deliberately retains the graph. Finalization attempts cleanup without raising and does not guarantee immediate unload. Closing a common view is not a substitute for closing this owner.

Parameters
Channel

Typed owner to close; do not race other operations on this owner.

Raised exceptions
Provider_Error

Disable/detach or native cleanup failure; a retained handle may require explicit cleanup retry.

Create_Config

  (Channel_ID : UCI_ID; Platform_ID : UCI_ID; Sensor_Location : Component_Location)
   return Health_Config

Platform_ID

Platform identity to pass to the provider.

Sensor_Location

Component location with meter offsets and location identity.

Return Value

Owned configuration retaining all supplied identity and location values.

Enable

procedure Enable (Channel : in out Health_Channel)

Explicitly enables the attached provider channel. Repeated Enable after success is a no-op; failure marks native lifecycle failed and requires cleanup rather than implying enabled service. Metadata may be registered before Enable.

Parameters
Channel

Attached owner to enable, or already enabled owner.

Raised exceptions
Provider_Error

Closed/failed owner, provider rejection/exception or native failure.

Health_Channel

type Health_Channel is limited private;

Limited typed owner, initially closed. Open attaches; Enable is explicit. Native state retains the Session/provider while this child needs it. Closing the public Session does not invalidate an existing channel. A weak common view does not keep this typed owner alive. Finalization attempts non-raising cleanup; failed detach can deliberately retain native resources for safety. Serialize lifecycle operations on the same Ada owner.

Health_Config

type Health_Config is private;

Owned configuration for attaching a typed HealthAndStatus channel; constructing it does not contact a provider.

Is_Open

function Is_Open (Channel : Health_Channel) return Boolean

Tests only local typed-channel handle ownership, not whether the channel is enabled or provider operations will succeed.

Parameters
Channel

Typed owner to inspect.

Return Value

True when its local native handle is nonnull.

Open

function Open (Parent : Session; Config : Health_Config) return Health_Channel

Attaches a HealthAndStatus channel, verifies its dynamic type and advertised channel capability, and publishes an owner only on success. Does not enable it. Metadata registration and capability queries are allowed while attached, before Enable. Native validation requires UTF-8 identity/location text without embedded NUL. Failed attachment/type validation attempts cleanup; uncertain detach retains the provider graph.

Parameters
Parent

Open IR Session whose provider supplies the child channel.

Config

Complete attachment identity and sensor location.

Return Value

Attached, not yet enabled, limited health-channel owner.

Raised exceptions
Provider_Error

Closed Session, invalid configuration text, provider attachment/capability/type failure or native failure.

Authentication values 1..7 mean subsystem, service, configuration-file, operational-software, mission-data-file, other-file and other-device authentication. Integrity 1..6 means configuration, bootloader, operational-software, mission-data-file, other-file and other integrity checks. File management 1..4 means configuration, operational- software, mission-data-file and other-file updates. State-command built-in testing that interrupts other functions, distinct from BIT that does not require a state change.

Limited controlled owner of a legacy native image stream. Default state is closed. Explicit Close reports errors; finalization provides non-raising cleanup fallback. Native ownership retains provider/session state as needed independently of the parent Ada Session object's lifetime.

Open_Image_Control

function Open_Image_Control
  (Parent : Session; Config : Image_Control_Config) return Image_Stream

Attach for Image commands, capabilities, common Channel operations and metadata, even when all advertised layout values are zero. Reuses the limited Image_Stream owner and its Stop/Close, pending-request and callback retention rules. Explicit Close is preferred to non-raising finalization. Start enables the channel only: no buffer factory, sample allocation or registration occurs. Enable is not evidence that acquisition has begun. Both Receive APIs (including frame leases) raise Provider_Error with a control-only diagnostic; no pixel view can be obtained from this owner.

Parameters
Parent
Config
Return Value
Raised exceptions
Provider_Error

Closed parent, invalid metadata or failed attach.

Pixel_Array

type Pixel_Array is array (Natural range <>) of Byte;

Unconstrained array of octets. Legacy received Frames own a one-based array of monochrome samples; borrowed views in child APIs have separate lifetime contracts and must not be treated as owned merely by this type.

Receive

function Receive (Object : Image_Stream; Timeout_Milliseconds : Natural := 0) return Frame

Receive a copied legacy frame using native size-discovery then copy calls. At most one task may call Receive on this stream at a time. Queued frames precede stopped/failure reporting. Serialize closure against this call.

Parameters
Object

Open legacy image stream whose next frame is consumed.

Timeout_Milliseconds

Wait duration in milliseconds; zero polls without waiting. A timeout neither stops the stream nor cancels provider work.

Return Value

Ada-owned pixels and selected scalar metadata for the next frame.

Raised exceptions
Timeout_Error

No frame becomes available within the wait.

Stream_Stopped

No queued frame remains and the stream is stopped.

Provider_Error

Closed/failed stream, size discovery failure or a frame outside this wrapper's Mono8 single-band metadata profile.

Stop

procedure Stop (Object : in out Image_Stream)

Stop acceptance and disable the stream with native cleanup/lifetime rules. Previously queued frames remain receivable before stopped reporting. This is not cancellation of every outstanding provider operation.

Stream_Counters

type Stream_Counters is record
   Frames_Received           : Counter;
   Frames_Dropped_Queue_Full : Counter;
   Malformed_Or_Unsupported  : Counter;
end record;

Snapshot of callback/rejection diagnostics, not successful Ada reads.

Record fields
Frames_Received

Incoming image callbacks counted before validation, including malformed data and queue-full drops.

Frames_Dropped_Queue_Full

Valid incoming frames rejected because the bounded receive queue has no space.

Malformed_Or_Unsupported

Malformed/unsupported callbacks and native callback failures rejected by the bridge, not timeout polls.

Stream_Stopped

Stream_Stopped : exception;

Receive found no queued frame and the native stream is stopped.

UCI_ID

type UCI_ID is private;

Ada-owned UUID and descriptive label. Predefined Ada equality compares both fields, including the label; matching UUID bytes alone need not make two Ada values equal. Pinned upstream equality also compares both fields.

UUID

type UUID is array (Natural range 0 .. 15) of Byte;

Exactly sixteen identifier bytes indexed zero through fifteen. These are binary identity bytes, not a UTF-8 label or a textual UUID encoding.
